about: THE PLUGIN CORPUS: good and bad adventure plugins that the authoring tool (tools/test_adventure_plugin.py) and the game's own loader (tests/unit/test_plugin_corpus.gd) both judge; each must reach the verdict and the first reason written here. Every case is BUILT by the test: its base folder copied, its own folder laid over it, its edits, additions and removals made, its files hashed, then zipped when it says zip. The recipe's words are listed under recipe.

recipe.base: a folder of this corpus copied first (good_minimal: what adventure_plugin.py new writes)
recipe.folder: a folder of this corpus laid over the base, file by file
recipe.edit: {file: {set: [{path, value}], remove: [path]}}: a JSON file changed; a path is a list of keys and list indexes (an index one past the end appends); a value {$repeat: [text, n]} is text n times, {$list: [value, n]} a list of n values, {$nest: n} n lists nested in each other
recipe.add: files written: {rel, text} | {rel, hex} | {rel, repeat: [text, n]} | {rel, png: [width, height]} (a PNG header) | {rel, link: target} (a symbolic link) | {rel, dirs: 1} (an empty folder) | {rel, prefix_hex} (bytes put before the file's own); count: n makes n of them, {n} in rel numbering them
recipe.hash_files: true: plugin.json given a files list with the SHA-256 of every other file, as export writes it
recipe.after: changes once hashed: {rel, append: text} | {rel, delete: true} | an add
recipe.zip: {top}: the plugin zipped (stored entries) under that top folder, its files in the order of the folder's walk; extra: raw entries added {name | name_hex, text | hex, method, flags, made_by, external, size (claimed, the bytes not), count}; zip64: true writes zip64 end records; raw_text: the zip file is this text
recipe.reason: the first problem, exactly; {game_version} is the game's version
recipe.reason_prefix: the first problem begins so (the JSON parsers' own words differ)

set.value: A low den under a hill.
{hero}, champion of the den after {count} wins.
Beat the keeper of the den.
Learn {title}, link {town} and ride on (+{life_bonus} life so far)
The Lore. An old keeper sits by the door and nods as you come near.
"They say the roads east of here are quiet this week," the keeper says.
"A merchant came through yesterday, pale as milk. He would not say what he saw."
"The wind has turned. The old folk say that means a wizard is on the move."
The keeper smiles. "Back for more tales? I have told you my best one."
"This place is older than the towns," the keeper says. "It stood here before the five wizards raised their castles."
"Whoever built it left no name. But travelers who rest here say they dream of a road that is on no map."
The keeper of The Lore told you its tale.
The Gift. Someone has left a bundle here, tied with a ribbon, and a note beside it.
The note reads: "For the traveler who needs it. Take it, and remember us kindly."
You untie the ribbon. Inside: five days of food, and a white amulet.
The bundle is gone, and so is the note. Only the ribbon is left.
The Healer. A healer in a gray cloak looks up from her herbs.
"I can lay a blessing on you for your next duel," she says, "or sell you bread for the road. You carry {food} days of food."
"A blessing already rests on you. Fight your duel first; then come back."
"I have no more blessings for you. One traveler may carry only so many from here."
Ask for a blessing ({price} gold, {uses_left} left)
She lays a hand on your brow. You will begin your next duel with five more life.
Buy bread for three days (10 gold)
You pay 10 gold. The bread is still warm. You now carry {food} days of food.
The Toll. A keeper with a halberd bars the way.
"100 gold opens the gate," the keeper says, "or one amulet. You carry {amulets}."
The keeper looks at your colors and lowers the halberd. "A green mage? Your kind pass free."
"Day {day} of your journey, and you are still on the road? Few last so long."
The keeper steps aside and the gate swings open.
The gate stands open for you now. The keeper nods you through.
Climb the gate tower and look around
From the tower you see the land for miles around, and mark it on your map.
The Gambler. A man with quick hands rattles three bone dice in a cup.
"50 gold a throw," he says. "Three ways to fall: nothing, 75, or 150. 5 throws, and then I pack up."
You put down {price} gold. The dice rattle and fall.
Low numbers. He sweeps your gold away with a shrug.
A fair throw! He counts out 75 gold.
Three sixes! He pays out 150 gold and looks at the dice twice.
The gambler has packed his cup and dice. "5 throws, I said. Luck needs its rest."
The Riddle. Words are cut deep into the rock, and they seem to wait for you.
"I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, rivers but no water. What am I?"
The rock stays cold and still. That was not the answer. Come back and try again.
The words glow, and a hollow opens in the rock: 100 gold lies inside, yours for the answer.
The words have faded. The rock has told its riddle and keeps no other.
The Collector. A traveler sits among open chests, every one full of cards sorted by color.
"I am looking for Llanowar Elves," the collector says. "I pay 150 gold for each copy, and I need 3."
The collector's eyes light up. "You have one! I can see it in your bag."
You have sold the collector {count} so far.
The collector takes {card} with both hands and counts out 150 gold.
"Every copy I wished for. My set is whole," the collector says, and closes the chests.
The Duelist. Ropes mark a square of trampled grass, and a crowd waits around it.
The champion leans on the ropes. "50 gold says you cannot beat me. Win, and you take 100. 3 bouts, no more."
The crowd roars. {foe} pays you 100 gold without a word.
{foe} pockets your wager. "Come back when you have learned something."
The ropes are down and the crowd has gone home. The champion has no more bouts in him.
The Shop. A trader has spread a blanket by the road, a few cards laid out on it under stones.
"One of each, and when they are gone they are gone," the trader says. "And if you carry a pair of Glasses of Urza, I pay 60 gold for it."
Look at the cards for sale
You pay {price} gold, and {card} is yours.
The trader counts out {price} gold for {card}.
The Quest. A woman waits here, turning a ring on her finger again and again.
"My brother lies sick, and no herb helps," she says. "Only Healing Salve could cure him. Will you find one for me?"
"Thank you. Any shop or dungeon may hold one. I will wait here, however long it takes."
"Have you found Healing Salve yet? He grows weaker."
She sees the card in your bag and catches her breath.
She presses 200 gold into your hands. "It is all we have. He will live, because of you."
"He is walking again," she says, and for the first time her hands are still.
A woman at The Quest asked you to bring her Healing Salve.
Brought Healing Salve to The Quest.
Bring Healing Salve to The Quest.
Done: Healing Salve was brought to The Quest.
The Traveler. A carter waits beside a cart with high wheels, the mule already in harness.
"100 gold, and I take you to the nearest town," the carter says. "No questions, no stops. You carry {gold}."
The Teacher. An old mage sits cross-legged on a flat rock, eyes closed, and speaks before you do.
"I teach one thing that can be carried, and one that cannot," the mage says. "Dwarven Pick, for 800 gold. And the long breath, which adds to your life in every duel."
The mage opens one eye. "Dwarven Pick is yours already. That lesson is done."
"The long breath has given you {life_bonus} more life so far. No one learns more than ten."
The mage speaks for an hour, and draws one sign in the dust. {title} is yours.
Take a lesson in the long breath ({price} gold, {uses_left} left)
You breathe as you are told until the stars come out. You will begin every duel with {life_bonus} more life than before you met the mage.
